**Describe the bug**
`offroad` can be triggered at the first evaluation timestep, and this affects the final aggregated driving metrics in `aggregate/metrics_results.txt`.

**To Reproduce**
1. Run:
   ```bash
   uv run alpasim_wizard +deploy=local wizard.log_dir=/data/$TASK_ID services.driver.image=$docker_image_name
   ```
2. Open `aggregate/metrics_results.txt` and `aggregate/metrics_unprocessed.parquet`.
3. Check whether `offroad` is already `1` at the first timestep.
4. Compare the aggregated results with the raw per-timestep metrics.

comments.body: > interesting. Do you happen to have the clipgt id or an image from the video? Hi @maximilianigl Here are the `metrics_unprocessed.parquet` and the corresponding video for this clip, might help with the investigation. [metrics_results.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26164993/metrics_results.txt) [metrics_unprocessed.parquet.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26165000/metrics_unprocessed.parquet.txt) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/534e3cc8-3861-40ea-9fdd-e631e50e8194

Looks like the map is just wrong here: Black lines denote road borders, blue lines denote lane borders. 
Short term for you, I'd recommend just removing this clip from the list (check the `csv` files under `data`).
On our side, we'll have to figure out how to:
a) catch something like this earlier
b) update the scenesets on an ongoing basis without creating chaos when we find problems like this.

Thanks for flagging this!

Thanks @maximilianigl 

Adding some additional context — this may not be fully accurate.

I haven’t gone through the relevant code in detail yet — I asked an AI to look into it, and it suggested that:

```
An inconsistency in the evaluation window definition causes the initial warm-up / prerun frame to be included in the offroad evaluation. Once offroad is triggered on that first frame, the aggregation truncates subsequent timesteps, ultimately skewing the overall driving score.
```

I’m not sure if this is accurate, but sharing it here in case it’s helpful.

Thanks! I think this is mostly correct, but the problem isn't the pre-run aggregation, it's that the car starts as "offroad" because the map thinks that the lane divider which the car is currently crossing is actually a _road_ border. 
So even if we exclude the pre-run frames, the metrics will be wrong because we'll (wrongly) flag the car as offroad on the first "driven" frame.

There have been a number of clips that we had to remove because the xodr format has some issues. My opinion is that, if this is indeed a map issue (I didn't look carefully at the data), we should bring this up with the team that manages the NuRec artifacts and remove it from the test suite.

title: Offroad metric may be counted at the first timestep and affect aggregated driving scores
